title: Mutation-induced structural and dynamic perturbations at the IL-17A-IL-17RA interface: Therapeutic insights from multi-replicate molecular dynamics simulations.
authors: Razzaq, Afsheen; Sardar, Madiha; Mushtaq, Mamona; Nur-E-Alam, Mohammad; Ghayur, Muhammad Nabeel; Ul-Haq, Zaheer
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多副本分子动力学模拟和MM/GBSA计算，系统分析了IL-17A-IL-17RA界面热点残基突变对复合物结构、动态和结合亲和力的影响，属于蛋白质结构相关的计算模拟研究，方法扎实且直接服务于蛋白-蛋白相互作用的结构机制解析。
abstract: The interaction between Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) and its receptor IL-17RA plays a key role in pro-inflammatory signal transduction and is implicated in the pathogenesis of inflammatory autoimmune diseases. Blocking this protein-protein interaction is a major approach to developing therapeutic agents to inhibit IL-17A-induced signaling. Predicting the consequences of mutations on structure and function in proteins can be accomplished by using computational methods, which are relatively inexpensive and rapid compared with experimental methods. Here, we used a multidimensional in silico approach to gain insight into the functional and thermodynamic consequences of targeted mutation of hotspot residues of IL-17A. The focus of our analysis was on the residues in the two chains that are equivalent to hotspot residues of the related cytokine, IL-17F, at positions 55 and 67 of chain B and 85 and 86 of chain A. Comprehensive analysis of the conformational dynamics, interaction profiles, and structural transitions of the four mutant variant systems (R55V, W67V, Y85I, and H86S) and the wild-type system was performed based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and Molecular Mechanics/Generalized Born Surface Area (MM/GBSA) calculations. A total of 3 mus simulations were performed: three 200 ns replicates for each of the wild-type and mutant complexes. Results from principal component analysis (PCA) and free energy landscape (FEL) analyses indicate conformational destabilization of the mutant systems. These findings help to elucidate the mechanisms of molecular interactions involved in the dynamics of cytokine-receptor interaction. Changes in these important PSN network parameters resulted in differences in hub connectivity and distribution of the links between the systems, which suggests allosteric perturbations and remodeling of the system in the interaction between IL-17A and IL-17RA when compared to the wild-type systems. The multiple-replica MD simulation protocol provided insight into how mutations affected the structure, contact networks, dynamics, and binding affinity of the IL-17A/IL-17RA complex, shedding light on the IL-17A downstream signaling cascades. Overall, this study provides a fundamental framework for designing therapeutic strategies to regulate IL-17A-mediated inflammatory diseases.
abstract_zh: 白细胞介素-17A（IL-17A）与其受体IL-17RA之间的相互作用在促炎信号转导中发挥关键作用，并参与炎症性自身免疫疾病的发病机制。阻断这种蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用是开发抑制IL-17A诱导信号传导的治疗药物的主要策略之一。通过计算方法预测突变对蛋白质结构和功能的影响是可行的，与实验方法相比，这些方法相对成本较低且速度较快。在此，我们采用多维计算机模拟方法，深入探讨IL-17A热点残基靶向突变的功能和热力学后果。我们的分析重点集中在两条链中与相关细胞因子IL-17F热点残基对应的残基，即链B的第55和67位以及链A的第85和86位。基于分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟和分子力学/广义Born表面积（MM/GBSA）计算，对四种突变变体系统（R55V、W67V、Y85I和H86S）及野生型系统的构象动态、相互作用谱和结构转变进行了全面分析。共进行了3微秒模拟：野生型和突变复合物各进行三次200纳秒重复。主成分分析（PCA）和自由能景观（FEL）分析结果表明，突变系统存在构象失稳。这些发现有助于阐明细胞因子-受体相互作用动态中涉及的分子相互作用机制。这些重要PSN网络参数的变化导致枢纽连接性和系统间链接分布的差异，这表明与野生型系统相比，IL-17A与IL-17RA相互作用中存在变构扰动和系统重塑。多重复MD模拟协议提供了突变如何影响IL-17A/IL-17RA复合物结构、接触网络、动态和结合亲和力的见解，揭示了IL-17A下游信号级联反应。总体而言，本研究为设计调节IL-17A介导炎症性疾病的治疗策略提供了基础框架。
